lines.text: My work book. Hinges for the Widow Tamsett. I'll walk them down when the road's back.
Tam's at the Hobb fair. He'll be back by second bell. He always is.
You've been to the depot. Don't tell me what you found. Just tell me if he was counting rope.
Ludd's forms say the forge went before Hobb did. It didn't save us. It hired us.
My shift log. Went to inspect the east face. Woke here beside the tool shelter.
Ground beyond the east face again. Don't recognize it. Leaving that face alone.
We prayed to the Banked Fire: keep it low, keep it fed, never let it go hungry. I've been watching your Core.
It took my cut and the girl from the Seams. Not the yard, not the kilns. Just the hands that could make you a rune.
My cutting book. Moll sent me to the quarry with her wheels. I knew she wanted me out of the mines. I still thought I'd be going back.
The stones you bring back hum when I first set them. I wait till they stop.
Moll stayed to hear the end of the song. Listen to the Core. It's all on one note.
Her observation book. The seams wouldn't hold for a drawing. She marked where they'd been.
She told me to take the charts to the town. There's no town. So I chart the rifts. Somebody should know.
Count the cracks over the Core. Five, and never the same shape twice. Her sky did that, at the end. I mark the rifts by date now.
Choose a world. I'll attune the key. I used to call that cartography.
She ruled a line from the Empty Chair to where the seams opened. I've finished it for her. It ends at your Core.
The waybook. I put those pins in myself. Red for the stations that stopped answering.
One white pin left. Tull's Cross. That's about where we're standing.
I know what you're fighting. I still teach you how. It's the only thing I'm good for.
Keep drilling. One day you'll fight something that isn't guarding anything. I'd like you ready for that one.
Form nine. Everything that floats. I signed the last one with nothing on it.
I sent Penk's lad to count rope. I don't know which side of the edge the rope shed was.
Things come in, they get logged, nothing goes out. I kept stores for a whole town once.
A smith, a quarry crew, a cutter, a chart-reader, a drill sergeant, a storesman. That's not a rescue. That's a muster roll.
Our Watch book. Over three thousand darks of observations. Once, an entry for every light in the sky.
There was a green light in our sky. I knew your light before I knew your face.
The Hinge kept us steady. Now I steady your keys, and I'm good at it.
The first keepers recorded the fall but never found where the light landed. I think we're standing on it.
My sowing book. I wrote it for whoever tended the garden next. I didn't think that would be me.
The kale took. It always does. The salt didn't come with us, so I salt the beds by hand.
'The Saltry gardens, with Neve Saltry and her fig.' She's on the south wall. She'll fruit if you leave her alone.
My casebook. I was the last case in it. I'm steadier here. The ground holds.
The Readers wrote it all down. I couldn't help the people in my casebook. I can still help you.
The ground holds here because something holds it. I can feel it underneath. It's very glad of you.
I've written my name inside your collar. Ama. In case you come back one day and can't find it.
Gran's recipes. Tide bread wants sea water. I use well water and salt. It's not the same, but it's bread.
That's the little one's hand at the end, copying out the bread. Gran made her.
The market half went on the ninth day. Gran had the little one at market all that week. I'll bake tide bread tomorrow.
Our Book of Things Taken. I gave you your name in it. I hoped you were trying to put something right.
I restore what you bring me. It's the only restoring here I can do honestly.
We prayed for you every day the cloister stood. I've kept on. The Patient Water doesn't stop because the answer is no.
We taught the Climber to novices who wouldn't wait their turn. I never imagined its voice would be kind.
The Readers' finding. You'll see I dissented. I said you'd know eventually.
It can't be bound while it's small. It must stand up first, and it won't until it's whole. Finish it. I'll keep the register.
Home is finished. It's still growing. I'll record the day it stands up.

known.text: %s. Hand me your kit; I'll see to it. I don't need to hear how it went.
%s, then. Leave the gear on the bench. It'll be ready by second bell.
Request done.
That's one more off the board.
%s, down. Put the stone in the bin. I won't ask what it was cut from.
%s. Leave any crystals by the shelter. I'll look them over when I've finished this cut.
Tier %s. Deeper every time. We went at the east face like that once.
More work for my bench. At least I still know how to do it.
Order filled. Set it by the bench; I'll sort it.
%s. Leave its stones a day. Let them finish humming.
%s. Bring me what you have and I'll set it.
Tier %s. The stones come back louder now. I wait longer before I cut.
%s. I'll mark it, with the date. Somebody should know where it was.
%s. It goes in the atlas. She'd want it written down properly.
A tier %s clear. I'll ink it in. I've stopped calling it new ground.
Inked in. I've left a margin for what was there.
More room in the atlas. It fills faster than I'd like.
You brought down %s. I've started keeping the names.
%s, fallen. I heard. Sit a while before you go to the Core.
Tier %s cleared. The home grows. I try not to look at the edges.
A tier %s clear. I know where some of those doors lead now.
More work. I'll do it. I'm starting to think that's what I'm here for.
%s, down. Good footwork. I taught you that, and I'd teach it again.
%s. Come and drill tomorrow. Keep your hands busy.
%s. Supplies go in the ledger. I'll leave the rest out.
%s, entered and filed. There's a box on the form for this now. I wish there weren't.
%s. Somewhere a light just went out. I used to write those down.
%s, fallen. I'll steady your next key.
%s. Come and sit by the kale a minute.
%s, fallen. I keep thinking about the gardens there. I hope someone sowed them.
%s. Let me see your hands. Steady enough.
%s. The ground there will be letting go. Drink this.
%s. I've kept a plate back. Eat first.
%s, fallen. Gran fed whoever came to the door. I'm trying to keep to that.
%s. I'll add it to the book tonight, Restorer, and a prayer after it.
%s, fallen. The Patient Water says keep praying. So I do, for them and for you.
%s. I'll enter the name beside the others.
%s, fallen. Bring me any relic it dropped. I'll catalog what remains.
You looked at me as though you were trying to place me. Sit down.
You come back a little quieter every time.
Dents and scorch. You asked me who made this. I did. You asked last time too.
You look worn. You didn't know my name at the door. It's Dessa. I'll keep saying it.
Let's choose the next rift together. I'll show you which ones you chose before.
I've checked the new routes. I know what I'm sending you toward.
